blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A feed mill mixes soy meal (44% protein) and corn (9% protein), s and c tons of each, and the mix's average protein must be at least 18%. Which row states the rule linearly?

options.says: The average is the weighted sum divided by the total; the 18 must be multiplied by s + c too.
Right: multiply the average by the total s + c, then collect the terms.

options.text: c = 0, since corn alone is below 18%
options.says: An average limits the mix, not each ingredient; soy's surplus makes room for corn.
This divides by variables, so it is not linear; multiply it out first.

origin.section: A Blend Rule Bounds an Average, and the Average Is Linear Once Multiplied by the Total

questions.stem: In a shipping LP, the only depot holds 60 spares and the regions need exactly 50 between them. The modeler writes the depot's row as out − in = 60. What does the solver report?

options.text: OPTIMAL, with 10 spares left on the shelf at the depot
options.says: An equation forces all 60 out of the depot; nothing can stay on the shelf.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with the extra 10 sent to the cheapest region
options.says: Each region's row is an equation, so no region can take more than it needs.

options.text: INFEASIBLE, since no flow can balance the depot's row
options.says: Right: the depot row must be ≤ because spares may stay; as an equation no flow fits.

options.text: UNBOUNDED, since the extra spares have nowhere to go
options.says: No flow satisfies every row, so the model is infeasible, not unbounded.

origin.section: A Flow Model Has One Balance Row per Node: What Comes In, Less What Goes Out

questions.stem: A five-year budget LP with carry-over leaves $2M unspent in its final year, while its first year was short of money. Why can the model not use that $2M?

options.text: The cash row is an inequality, so the model chose to waste it
options.says: The inequality lets money lapse, but the model would spend it if any row allowed it.

options.text: Carry-over moves money forward only, and no year comes after the last
options.says: Right: r links year y to y + 1; nothing carries money back to earlier years.

options.text: Discounting makes final-year money worth nothing to the model
options.says: Discounting lowers later value, but a positive value per $ is still worth spending.

options.text: Carried amounts must be equal in every year, so they cancel out
options.says: Each year has its own carry variable; their values differ.

origin.section: Multi-Period Carry-Over Is a Stock Variable That Links Each Year's Cash Row to the Next

concepts: a depot row written as an equation
money left in the final year of a plan
